maya: Nightly evals just flagged a pretty noticeable regression on the structured-output suite after v17.1 bring-up. JSON fields truncated and some keys missing on several prompts.
ci-bot: nightly-eval v17.1 - structured-output - FAILED (regression delta +9.8% vs baseline v17.0) :x:
maya: sample failing prompt + generation below.
maya: ```
PROMPT: Generate JSON metadata for an article with fields: title, author, summary, tags
EXPECTED: {\"title\":\"...\",\"author\":\"...\",\"summary\":\"...\",\"tags\":[...]}
V17.1 OUTPUT: {\"title\":\"How we scaled inference\",\"author\":\"S. Patel\",\"summary\":\"We...\",\"tags\":
V17.0 OUTPUT: {\"title\":\"How we scaled inference\",\"author\":\"S. Patel\",\"summary\":\"We built...\",\"tags\":[\"inference\",\"runtime\"]}
```
sahil: :eyes: interesting. looks like the tokens for 'tags' array are being cut off mid-token. could be tokenizer merge table change or kv cache cutoff.
liam: I ran a quick diff on tokenization between v17.0 and v17.1 for that prompt.
liam: v17.0 tokens: ["{","\\\"title\\\"",":","\\\"How","we","scaled","inference\\\"",...]
liam: v17.1 tokens: ["{","\\\"title\\\"",":","\\\"How we scaled inference\\\"",...\"\\\"tags\",\"\\\":\"] -> our BPE merged 'How we scaled inference' into one token but split 'tags':\" into two leading to unexpected sequence length estimates.
anita: also seeing slightly higher per-token latency in v17.1 quantized kernel (int4 path); that could be causing batching window to chop the suffix in some configs.
eva: I reproduced locally with quantized build and non-quantized; truncation only appears on int4 path with continuous batching enabled.
maya: so two hypotheses: tokenizer merge table changed (merge/merge-vocab) OR kv/batching code when combined with int4 runtime cuts final chunk.
sahil: can we repro deterministically by forcing batch size=1 and disabling prefix cache?
liam: yes, with BATCH=1 + prefix_cache=off the output is intact even on int4. with batching=8 truncated. suggests batching/windowing bug.
anita: I dumped kv lengths and found off-by-one in the prefix flush boundary inside int4 kernel path. suspect kernel metadata rounding.
maya: plan: 1) revert v17.1 autoscaler to v17.0 kernel for canary traffic 2) reproduce locally with instrumented kv boundaries 3) run tokenizer diff on merge tables 4) add a targeted unit test for batching flush on int4.
ci-bot: deploy request created: rollback v17.1 -> v17.0-canary (PR #4821) :rocket:
deploy-bot: rolling back canary now, expected 5m to stabilize.
sahil: I'll own the int4 kernel trace and add assert for kv flush size.
liam: I'll export tokenizer merge table diff and open issue if merges were updated without backward compat policy.
eva: I'll extend nightly eval to include a small structured-output corpus focused on arrays to catch this earlier.
maya: good. let's reconvene after rollback stabilizes. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml for visibility.
